title: Wave Core (W-Core)
summary: Core's own synth for leads, pads and drones: from one screaming saw to a wide, slow cloud.
steps: On a melody or pad track, open the track menu and choose Replace instrument > Synth.
Start from a preset (the button at the top): each one is a whole sound for a style, with its mood.

Make it yours: the preset menu's "Save this sound as yours…" keeps every knob, the drift and the mood; it then appears under Yours. Compare goes back to the sound you had before the last preset, and again.
Lead plays one note at a time and can slide between notes (Glide); Pad plays chords. The preset sets it; the Lead/Pad button changes it.
Drag across the wave to change what the note is made of: Buzzy is the classic lead, Round is soft.
Spread makes it wide (up to seven detuned waves); Stack adds an octave under or over it. Fine tune moves the pitch by up to a semitone, to sit with a sample.
Tone sets how dark it is, Bite how much it screams; Contour and Bloom make it open on each note.
Swell and Fade: short for leads, seconds for pads. Decay and Sustain shape a held note: Sustain 0 makes a pluck that dies by itself while the key is down.
Colour adds new sources: Noise (Colour from dark to bright) for air and wind, FM with its Ratio for metallic, bubbly tones. Zap makes the pitch fall into each note (Zap time sets how fast).

Grain cuts a sound into tiny pieces and plays many at once: a cloud, a shimmer or a frozen texture. Grain sound (on the Grain card) picks a sample of your library to cut, or Wave for the synth's own wave. Size is each piece's length, Density how many start each second, Position where in the sound they start, Scan how fast that place moves (0 freezes it), Scatter how random they are.
Pick a mood for what comes after the synth: Echo 3/16, Ping-pong 1/4, Slap 1/8, Cathedral, Gated or Grit. Dry takes it away.

examples.title: Fullspeed Saw
examples.text: Bass: a hi-tech rolling bass copied from one of Diogo's bass samples by ear-matching, made only by the synth. The Bass group has nine of these (psy saws, hi-tech, dark, deep).

examples.title: Sunrise Screamer
examples.text: The full-on screamer lead, with the 3/16 psy echo.

examples.title: Forest Glide
examples.text: One saw that slides between notes: progressive and twilight lines.

examples.title: Swamp Siren
examples.text: Dark and screaming, with an octave under it: dark psycore lines.

examples.title: Rusted Hoover
examples.text: Wide and rolling, a little dirty, moving over two bars.

examples.title: Acid Needle
examples.text: A 303-style acid line with a short slide and a slap echo: hi-tech.

examples.title: Static Riser
examples.text: Hard and wide, an octave up, drifting over four bars: FX lines.

examples.title: Cathedral Fog
examples.text: A soft, wide pad that swells in, in a huge space: slambient.

examples.title: Abyss Drone
examples.text: Hold one note for a whole section: a dark drone that moves over eight bars.

examples.title: Night Pluck
examples.text: A short, dark pluck that dies while the key is held: dark psycore stabs.

examples.title: Bubble Metal
examples.text: FM at an odd ratio with a fast zap: the metallic, bubbly hi-tech line.

examples.title: Laser Zap
examples.text: Two octaves of pitch fall in 40 ms on every note: hi-tech lasers.

examples.title: Ghost Wind
examples.text: A soft pad with breathy noise inside it: slambient.

examples.title: Glass Cloud
examples.text: Grain: a shimmering cloud of long, scattered grains for breakdowns. Pick a sound in Grain sound to cloud it.

styles.why: Buzzy saw leads with a 3/16 echo; glide for progressive.
Low Tone, more Bite, an octave stacked below.
Acid lines with Bite near the top, short slap echoes.
Pad mode, long Swell and Fade, Drift over many bars, the Cathedral mood.
